investigations.name: fluid-resuscitation
investigations.title: Fluid resuscitation after hemorrhage
investigations.objective:
After a severe right-leg hemorrhage, does a closed-loop MAP-targeted infusion
preserve blood volume and arterial pressure compared with no treatment, and
does the infused compound (saline vs whole blood) matter?
investigations.claim: Both treated arms end with more blood volume (+78 mL) and a higher MAP (+2.2 mmHg) than the untreated arm, but saline and whole blood are indistinguishable over 10 minutes.

investigations.name: hemorrhage-severity-sweep
investigations.title: Hemorrhage severity sweep
investigations.objective:
How do blood loss, heart rate and mean arterial pressure over 10 minutes
depend on the severity of a right-leg hemorrhage in the StandardMale patient?
investigations.claim: Blood loss and heart rate rise steadily with severity, while MAP stays within 1.1 mmHg of its start up to severity 0.4 and falls 7-17 mmHg from severity 0.6 upward.

investigations.name: patient-cohort
investigations.title: Hemorrhage across the shipped patients
investigations.objective:
Does the same right-leg hemorrhage (severity 0.8, 10 minutes) produce the
same qualitative response in all 21 patients that ship with Pulse, and how
does the fraction of blood lost depend on the patient's starting blood volume?
investigations.claim: All 21 shipped patients bleed and compensate the same way, and the fraction of blood lost falls with starting blood volume (Spearman rho = -0.91).
